top.text: When opponents push or rush to Ginting's rear backhand, Ginting loses the point within two shots 10% of the time (n=90, 95% CI 5%-18%); typical pros lose 25% after the same shot (difference -15 points, 95% CI -20 to -6, n=1376).

At 18+ in a game, when opponents push or rush, wherever it lands, Ginting loses the point within two shots 6% of the time (n=35, 95% CI 2%-19%); typical pros lose 22% after the same shot (difference -16 points, 95% CI -21 to -3, n=843).

When opponents push or rush, wherever it lands, Ginting loses the point within two shots 16% of the time (n=267, 95% CI 12%-21%); typical pros lose 23% after the same shot (difference -7 points, 95% CI -11 to -2, n=5417).

summary.text: Pushes and rushes to Ginting's rear backhand win fewer points than they do against typical pros.

xp.caveat: Read this first: xP from shot and position data has no signal mid-rally in elite singles (holdout AUC 0.50 on strokes that did not end the rally). The same features reach AUC 0.79 only on final strokes, where the task is classifying how an already-decisive stroke ends (winner or error), not predicting a rally. Nothing in this section is a working expected-points model.
